text:
kevin: quick async standup — kernel + batching + KV cache bench notes. what i did / blockers / today

maria: did a focused pass on the attention kernel rewrite yesterday. moved index math into the aligned path, reduced branch mispredictions. baseline microbench (single-GPU) shows ~8% p99 latency drop on seq=512. no regressions on fp16 tests.

sam: what I did: landed batching logic for variable-length inputs (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/482). added dead-slot compaction to reduce wasted slots when sequences end early.

sam: blocker: noticed occasional KV cache thrash when many short requests hit the same host — cache eviction policy seems to thrash under mixed seq distributions. reproducer in bench harness.

priya: ping @sam — can you paste the reproducer command? I want to try with the new prefetch flag.

sam: sure — run: `./bench/run.sh --model gptx-small --seq 64 --concurrency 80 --duration 120 --seed 42` then tail the server logs. failing workload pattern attached in the harness (short-heavy.json).

alexa: quick numbers from my run with `kv-prefetch=true` and the latest kernel patch:
```
seq=64 conc=80 tokens/s=18.4k p50=21ms p95=74ms p99=210ms
cache_hit_rate=0.78 eviction_rate=0.005
```

alexa: with prefetch=false (same code):
```
seq=64 conc=80 tokens/s=15.9k p50=24ms p95=92ms p99=330ms
cache_hit_rate=0.62 eviction_rate=0.018
```

kevin: nice delta. suggests prefetch + compaction helps. can we get a run with seq distribution mixed (64/256/1024) to reflect prod?

maria: I ran mixed-dist on the perf pool (gpu-a7-07) overnight. short summary: kernel improvements give consistent p50 improvements across all seqs; batching changes help throughput for mixed workloads but increase worst-case tail if eviction spikes. attaching perf summary link: https://perf.redwood/bench/17695-kernel-mix (internal).

priya: code review ping @maria @kevin on PR #499 — adds a configurable eviction watermark + prefetch toggle. looking for quick +1s so we can canary.

kevin: reviewing now. main question: what's the default for eviction watermark? should we be conservative (0.85) or aggressive (0.6) for dedicated customers?

maria: default is 0.8 in the PR, but we've been testing 0.7-0.85. my recommendation: 0.8 for hosted, allow tenant override for Dedicated.

sam: ops note: when we flip to 0.8 on canary, watch for increased disk io on the remote-evict path (we saw a spike yesterday on the int pool).

ci-bot: build #2145 for PR 499 succeeded — integration tests for kv and batching passed. :white_check_mark:

alexa: next steps for today: 1) kevin to finish review on #499, 2) sam to add reproducer to the CI matrix, 3) priya to schedule a canary rollout for staging with kv-prefetch=true, 4) maria to summarize mixed-dist numbers in the perf doc.

kevin: ack — will finish review by EOD and add comments. if all green we can canary tomorrow morning and monitor cache_hit_rate + p99.

sam: I'll add the reproducer job and a quick alert on eviction_rate > 0.01.

priya: scheduling canary for 0800 PST tomorrow, will include a rollback window and smoke tests. tagging oncall in the canary doc.

maria: Thanks everyone — drop small follow-ups here. :thumbsup:
